stages.request: Item costs are written to the data file as decimal strings like "2.50", and our finance import can't read them. Please replace `items.<sku>.unit_cost` with `items.<sku>.cost_cents`, an `integer` number of cents (250 for $2.50), and raise the data file's `version` to 2. Files written at version 1 must keep working: they should open as before and come out in the new form the next time they are saved.

I mistyped a transfer as `stockroom transfer BOLT-M6 5 A1 A1`, and afterwards A1 showed 5 more bolts than it had before; `stockroom check` then reported a mismatch for BOLT-M6 at A1.

A transfer whose source and destination are the same location should be refused, changing nothing, with a `same location` error: `cannot transfer within one location: <code>` (for my typo, `cannot transfer within one location: A1`).

When scripting against the library, `Inventory.on_hand(sku)` only gives me a grand total. Please make it return a `dict` mapping each location code to the quantity held there, leaving out locations that hold none of the item, and add `Inventory.total(sku)` returning the grand total as an `int` (0 when nothing is held). Both should refuse an unknown SKU with the usual `unknown item: <sku>` error.

Our scanner app logs which movement each library call produced. Today `Inventory.receive`, `issue` and `transfer` return a quantity and `adjust` returns the change; please make all four return the `seq` of the movement they record instead.

Our warehouse system imports the movement log from the data file and needs every line to touch exactly one location. Record each movement as lines in which `movements[].location`, a `string` naming that one location, and `movements[].delta`, a signed `integer` (positive for goods coming in, negative for goods going out), replace `movements[].qty`, `movements[].from` and `movements[].to`. A transfer becomes two lines, out of the source and into the destination, sharing the transfer's `seq`.

Raise the file `version` to 3; version 1 and 2 files must still open and be rewritten in the new form when saved.

Some of our bins are small. Let locations have an optional capacity: `stockroom add-location C3 --capacity 50` on the command line and a `capacity` argument to `Inventory.add_location`. Without one, a location has no limit.

A receive or transfer that would leave a location holding more units than its capacity, counting every item stored there, must change nothing and be refused with a `location full` error: `location <code> is full: capacity <capacity>, would hold <units>` (for example `location C3 is full: capacity 50, would hold 60`). Keep the capacity on the location in the data file as `capacity`, null when there is no limit.
